CheckTitle: Ensure cross-account IAM roles do not grant broad ReadOnlyAccess policies
Description: IAM roles configured for cross-account access should grant only the minimum permissions required for their purpose. Broad read-only access (ReadOnlyAccess) across all services may expose sensitive data in other AWS services (S3, Secrets Manager, SSM Parameter Store) to the trusted external account.
Risk: Cross-account roles with broad read-only access can expose sensitive configuration data, secrets, and resource metadata to the trusted account. Even read-only access can enable reconnaissance that leads to targeted attacks against the account.
Remediation: Restrict cross-account roles to the specific actions and resources needed by the trusted party. Add conditions such as aws:PrincipalOrgID to limit assumption to trusted organizational accounts. Avoid granting ReadOnlyAccess broadly across all services.
SeverityBasis: AWS IAM documentation — Security best practices in IAM (grant least privilege, including for cross-account roles); NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 AC-6 (Least Privilege), AC-4 (Information Flow Enforcement). Medium severity reflects read-only nature — no direct modification capability, but broad read access enables data exposure and reconnaissance. Severity is assigned by the framework's three-tier classification model defined in docs/severity_classification_model.md.
AuthoritativeSource: AWS IAM documentation — Cross-account access; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5
CISControl: N/A — cross-account role scoping is not individually enumerated in CIS AWS 3.0.0
